We have search results with two templates. Need the one that when applied to the given molecule reproduces the SN2 reaction (halide displaced by nucleophile). The description: "C-N formed and C-Cl gone breaking a 'halide' functional group". Our target molecule: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. It contains a side chain with CN4CC(F)C4 (a tertiary amine with fluorine). The SN2 likely is substitution of a halide (Cl) by a nucleophile (maybe amine). But the molecule currently has no halide; maybe the retrosynthetic step is to break a C-N bond to generate a halide precursor? Actually retrosynthesis: we need to find a template that when applied to the molecule (target) gives precursors, i.e., reverse of SN2: break C-N bond to form C-Cl (halide) and nucleophile (amine). So template should be SN2 reverse: C-N formed, C-Cl broken. The template likely has functional_groups_broken: halide, formed: amine. The search gave two templates. Need to check which matches our molecule. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching with each template_id? We have template_hash but need template_id? The search result includes reaction_id and template_hash. The tool expects template_id (string). Possibly template_id is the reaction_id? Or maybe template_id is the hash? The description says "template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash) as an integer". So likely reaction_id is the template ID integer. So we have IDs 3196 and 1321.

We need to see which template matches our molecule. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching with each ID.
